status: No blocking finding in the reviewed MP ActiveCheck, movement-start and per-value sustain-policy changes. Actor-lifetime ownership remains separately unresolved.
scope: Read-only source/test review against the packaged v0.12.2 source. No build, game access or source edit. Line endings were normalized only for the review diff; fingerprints bind original bytes.

tests.verification: Read the existing author-run log and test source; did not execute another run.

checks.result: MpGauge requires supported maximum, finite readback, integer0..255. Zero explicitly rejects a new MP-only reward but pauses an existing reward; missing/malformed data waits.

WasUsable stores the prior resource observation. Both interval endpoints must be usable, and intervals longer than one second are not charged for ActiveCheck effects. Return from missing/zero gauge triggers immediate sustain; it does not retroactively charge the unavailable interval.
General control-timer opt-out remains effective, while resource unusability still pauses MP time. Definitions without ActiveCheck retain previous accounting.
Established monitor/sustain and same-effect Extend require current usability. Extensions remain queued and unpaid until useful. Unestablished native acknowledgements retain the prior exception.

Stop/restore/deferred-end/deferred-restore still use existing control, role, ownership and toggle-readback gates, not ActiveCheck. Losing MP maximum cannot alone block disabling the owned toggle. Retry and settlement code is unchanged.
ActiveEffects reports resource pause reason independently of the general control-timer preference.

The three timed movement rewards remain Sora-only. ReadRestorableValue requires finite readback accepted by the current FeatureDefinition.IsValidValue range/choice contract. Both originals are checked before the first write; the second is rechecked after the awaited first write. Missing or out-of-policy second values enter existing partial cleanup without a second command. This closes the previously noted out-of-policy startup gap. Moon Jump correctly describes height/fall limits.

Read the actual supported-role/zero/missing/NaN/fraction/out-of-range/capability cases, both sample endpoints, recovery and extension, timer opt-out, backward clock, long gaps, cleanup retries and external ownership changes. Program registers both new suites.

Read the new minimum-minus1/maximum-plus1 and concrete walk100/run100/jump1200/fall0 cases, exact inclusive policy endpoints with successful restoration, and second-original out-of-range after first awaited command. The existing author-run log now reports1643/0; this reviewer did not build.

checks.topic: Per-value sustain policy and ongoing movement usability
checks.result: All three movement rewards now use MovementReadiness as ActiveCheck. Missing/out-of-policy values pause sampled time, whole-effect sustain and extensions. Each restoring OwnedValue additionally checks its freshly read live value with FeatureDefinition.IsValidValue immediately before dispatch and before adopting it as Original. This catches a second scalar changed during an earlier awaited sustain command. Restore=false behavior remains unchanged; cleanup is not gated on current usability.

Read tests for runtime walk100/run100/jump1200/fall0, missing readbacks, paused duration, valid-range recovery without retroactive charge, valid post-script Original restoration, external-value preservation, second-command await race, and unchanged non-restoring sustain. The current author-run log reports1687/0; no reviewer build.

limitations: Host observations and native command execution are separate; this does not prove atomic resource availability for every native write.
No live MP gameplay or Twitch service was tested by this reviewer.
Timed movement ownership still cannot distinguish equal-valued replacement Actors, including Sora-to-Sora. Native manual support is separate.
An arbitrary future ActiveCheck delegate must itself remain read-only and exception-safe; this review checks the supplied MpGauge implementation.

Existing value-based ownership uses a tolerance and cannot identify an external writer that restores the same or sufficiently close value. These gates do not introduce an Actor generation token or an atomic host/native compare-and-write.
